sections.html:
Property tax in Mason County passes through three Shelton offices. The Treasurer takes in the money, the Assessor determines value, and the Board of Equalization settles disputes. All use North Fifth Street addresses and share the county number 360-427-9670. Callers in Belfair can reach the Treasurer at 360-275-4467.

The Treasurer is on the second floor of Building 1, 411 N 5th Street, staffed 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, closed legal holidays. A drive-up drop box waits in the alley. Mail goes to the Mason County Treasurer's Office, PO Box 429, Shelton, WA 98584-0429. Dial extension 475 for the Treasurer and extension 491 for the Assessor. The county has an online tax search called TaxSifter, and card payments (Visa, MasterCard, Discover, American Express) are accepted at the counter, online, or over the phone through Point N Pay, subject to a convenience fee under RCW 36.29.190.

Mason County has one incorporated city, Shelton, which is also the seat. Most residents live in unincorporated places such as Belfair, Allyn, Grapeview, Hoodsport, Skokomish and Union, and part of Olympic National Park and Olympic National Forest lies inside the county.

  • Population in July 2025: 71,165, up 8.3% since April 2020.
  • Owners live in 82.3% of homes, so your competition is mostly other owners' listings.
  • A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $411,800.
  • Building permits in 2025: 204.

The tax comes due in two payments, April 30 and October 31. A mailed payment is on time only if the postmark falls on or before the due date. Postal Service postmarks can lag, so send yours early. Late charges begin the day after a due date.

The schedule is set in RCW 84.56.020. For a residence with up to four units, delinquent tax draws nine percent annual interest and no penalty. For all other property the interest is twelve percent, with a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1.

One side note for owners of several parcels: someone who paid a DNR fire patrol assessment on more than one Mason County parcel may be due a refund from the state Department of Natural Resources. Requests are due by December 31, 2026.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Mason County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeals go to the Board of Equalization, 411 N 5th Street, Shelton, WA 98584-3466. Whichever is later sets your deadline: July 1 of the assessment year or the thirtieth day after the date on the Assessor's Notice of Change of Value. Mason County uses the 30-day rule in RCW 84.40.038. To get blank forms, ask the clerk at 360-427-9670 extension 268.

Deadlines can shift from year to year. In 2026 the Assessor dated its real property notices late, which pushed the appeal window into October. Do not rely on a calendar date from memory. The deadline for your case is printed on the notice.

The Board was created under chapter 84.48 RCW and works independently of the Assessor. It seats three members and two alternates on staggered three-year terms, and neither elected officials nor their employees may serve. It also hears appeals when the Assessor denies a senior citizen exemption. The county posts forms for real property, personal property, current use, senior exemption review, late filing exceptions and requests to reconvene the Board.

sections.h2: Relief programs and what you repay at sale
sections.html:
The Assessor administers five programs, two of which you must repay when you sell. Qualifying owners can choose among:

  • The senior citizen and disabled persons exemption, open at 61, on retirement for disability, or to a qualifying veteran.
  • A deferral for owners 60 or older, or retired for disability, where the state pays the tax and the deferred amount accrues 5% simple interest.
  • A limited-income deferral of the second-half installment, for owners with five years in the home, with applications due September 1.
  • A grant for the widow or widower of a veteran.
  • Current use classification for open space, farm and agricultural land, and designated forest land.

Both deferrals must be repaid once the home sells, the owner dies or the house is no longer the primary residence. That puts the deferred tax and interest on your closing statement, so request the balance from the Assessor before you list. The exemption has no repayment.

ESSB 6162 starts with the 2027 tax year. The Assessor describes it as raising income thresholds, giving a full exemption from the state school levy, and lowering the veteran disability rating needed from 80% to 40%. A $70,000 combined disposable income limit is listed for 2027, and renewals are required every three years. The statute is RCW 84.36.381.

A parcel in the current use program is assessed at a reduced level because it is kept as open space, farm land or forest land. The application fee is $600 per parcel and is nonrefundable. Designated forest land needs a timber management plan with the first application, and again when the property is conveyed or sold.

That second filing lands on the seller's side of the table. If you hold forest land in Mason County, ask the Assessor what the buyer must file before the deed is signed. The Mason Conservation District offers technical and financial help to landowners, and the county page links the DNR's Find Your Forester tool.

sections.h2: If Mason County taxes are already behind
sections.html:
Call the Treasurer's Foreclosure Deputy at 360-427-9670 extension 485 before a parcel reaches a tax judgment sale. The county posts a foreclosure information sheet, a minimum bid sheet, public notices of judgment sales and a link to Bid4Assets, the online auction site.

The Treasurer points owners to three outside resources: the Washington Homeownership Resource Center at 1-877-894-4663, which gives free referrals, a nonprofit counseling agency called American Financial Solutions, and the Assessor's Office, which can say whether the senior or deferral programs fit a home with back taxes. Under RCW 84.56.020 the treasurer may arrange payment agreements for past due years, and an owner of limited income who occupies the home may ask for interest and penalties to be waived near the three-year mark while a foreclosure action is pending.

If you decide to sell, get the payoff figure first and let escrow pay it at closing. A cash buyer can often close fast enough to beat a judgment sale date.

sections.h2: Excise tax for a Mason County seller
sections.html:
Most of the time the seller bears Washington's real estate excise tax. When a seller leaves it unpaid, liability shifts to the buyer and a lien can follow. Payment is owed as of the sale date, and your deed, affidavit and check are presented to the county treasurer. Wait a month and 6% interest accrues from the sale date, the figure for both 2026 and 2027.

On sales starting January 1, 2027, state rates published by the Department of Revenue run 1.1% through $551,000, 1.28% through $1,551,000, 2.75% through $3,051,000 and 3.0% beyond that. A local rate is added. For the local figure and recording steps, call the Treasurer.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Mason County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Visit the Treasurer's Office on the second floor of Building 1, 411 N 5th Street, Shelton, weekdays from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. A drive-up drop box sits in the alley.

faqs.q: What is the Mason County deadline to appeal my value?
faqs.a: Whichever is later, July 1 or 30 days after the date on your Notice of Change of Value. Look at the notice itself, since mailing dates vary from year to year.

faqs.q: Do I have to repay a Mason County property tax deferral when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The deferred tax plus interest is owed at sale, at the owner's death, or when the home stops being the primary residence. Get the balance from the Assessor before listing.

faqs.q: Who handles tax foreclosure in Mason County?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Foreclosure Deputy, at 360-427-9670 extension 485. The county's foreclosure page links to the minimum bid sheet and the Bid4Assets auction site.

faqs.q: Can I pay Mason County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, with Visa, MasterCard, Discover or American Express, at the counter, online or by phone. Every card payment carries a convenience fee.
